items.title: Oilers’ Mattias Ekholm out at least one week with upper-body injury
items.summary: Ekholm appeared to hit his head on the ice and was helped off the ice by his teammates.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Stephen R. Sylvanie-USA TODAY Sports Edmonton Oilers’ defenseman Mattias Ekholm will be out at least one week after he suffered an upper-body injury during Thursday’s game against the Carolina Hurricanes , head coach Mike Babcock told reporters after the game. Ekholm, 36, was injured just seconds into the third period after Hurricanes’ forward William Carrier delivered a hit in the Oilers’ end. The Edmonton blueliner appeared to hit his head on the ice and was slow to get up, and his teammates helped him off the ice. He finished the game with 14:16 of ice time, and the Oilers would defeat the Hurricanes 6-5 in a shootout. Both Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl recorded five points and factored in on all five of Edmonton’s goals. McDavid now has 31 points and has become the fourth player in NHL history to register 30 points through the first 10 games of a season . Ekholm, a native of Borlange, Sweden, has one goal and two assists for three points , and has averaged 21:45 of ice time through 10 appearances. Now in his 15th NHL season, the 6-foot-4 defender has 93 goals and 311 assists for 404 points in 976 career regular-season games with the Oilers and Nashville Predators . He also has 13 goals and 47 assists for 60 points in 125 career Stanley Cup Playoff games. He was part of both of Edmonton’s Stanley Cup Final runs in 2024 and 2025, and was also part of the Predators’ 2017 appearance. Ekholm is in the first season of a three-year contract extension signed in October 2025. He was acquired by the Oilers ahead of the 2023 NHL Trade Deadline , with Edmonton sending Tyson Barrie, along with draft picks and a prospect to Nashville. The Oilers are now 8-1-1 through their first 10 games of the 2026-27 campaign.

items.title: Devin Cooley’s masterpiece sparks Flames to win over Wild

A sampling from the NHL’s Most Interesting Man, who two days earlier went viral trying to explain the difference between playing with a conscious and an unconscious brain: “Yeah, just a lot of thoughts popping in the head, and say like, ‘you know, you can move on - you don't have to stick around here, go away,” he explained, wide-eyed and abnormally loud, to the assembled press. “And then sometimes the thoughts stick around and they're in your head for a while, and you're like, ‘OK, you can stick around, you can hang out here. It gave the Flames their third win in four games, which is a bounce-back few saw coming after the team was outscored by more than a couple touchdowns their first five games. items.title: ‘It’s just not real’: McDavid makes even more history in Oilers’ shootout win
items.summary: It’s just obscene what Connor McDavid is doing in his 29-year old season, ripping through the competition even more surgically than in years past. On Thursday, he hit yet another milestone.
items.body: EDMONTON — It’s the curse that rides shotgun next to the absolute blessing of watching the sport’s finest talent on a nightly basis. Or playing with that player. After another five-point night by Connor McDavid , in a thrilling 6-5 win over Carolina on Thursday, this scribe was lucky enough/dutybound to perform the task of trying to find a new angle for the “How great a player is Connor McDavid?” storyline. I could publish of book my columns on this topic (it wouldn’t sell), and McDavid isn’t even 30 years old yet. And, of course, his teammates get to relive the weekly task of standing in front of a group of reporters, each of us trying to find a new route into the most travelled destination in Edmonton hockey history. AG — after Gretzky — of course. “Connor broke a Gretzky record: 31 points now in this first 10 games,” a media member said, inside a question for Leon Draisaitl. “Those are video-game numbers!” Draisaitl had five points Thursday as well. But there he stood, being asked the “How awesome is Connor?” question for about the 2,000th time in his career. “What do you want me to say? It's just not real,” Draisaitl said. “He's maybe the greatest player to ever play, in my books. It’s a pleasure to share the ice with him, a pleasure to learn from him every day. He deserves everything.” With a five-point night, McDavid set an Oilers record for the most points through 10 games in a season with 31, surpassing Wayne Gretzky in 1984-85. And McDavid is one of just four players — alongside Gretzky, Mario Lemieux (three times) and Mike Bossy — to start a season with 30 points in the first 10 games. items.title: Red Wings’ John Gibson leaves game with upper-body injury
items.summary: Gibson left the Red Wings’ game against the Canucks with an upper-body injury and did not return.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images The Detroit Red Wings announced on social media that goaltender John Gibson left Thursday night’s game against the Vancouver Canucks with an upper-body injury. He would not return. Gibson did not take the ice for the third period. However, he did not face any shots in the second frame, as the Red Wings outshot the Canucks 13-0. Gibson had stopped four of five shots in the opening period. Michal Postava, whom the team called up from their AHL affiliate in Grand Rapids one day earlier, stopped seven of eight shots faced in his NHL debut, and the Red Wings defeated the Canucks 5-2. Gibson, 33, is 2-3-1 with an .871 save percentage (SV%) and 3.35 goals against average (GAA) in seven appearances in 2025-26. Through 13 NHL seasons, the Pittsburgh native has a 235-242-68 record with an .909 SV% and 2.88 GAA in 570 career regular-season games with Detroit and Anaheim Ducks . He’s also appeared in 26 career Stanley Cup Playoff games, where he’s posted an 11-13 record with a .912 SV% and 2.80 GAA. Gibson was selected by the Ducks in the second round of the 2011 NHL Entry Draft. Across four AHL seasons, all with the Norfolk Admirals, he went 34-23-8 with a .921 SV% and 2.38 GAA in 70 appearances. He also spent two seasons playing junior hockey in the Ontario Hockey League with the Kitchener Rangers, where he went 38-19-1 with a .928 SV% and 2.60 GAA in 59 career games. The Red Wings are now 4-3-3 with 11 points through their first 10 games of the season.

items.summary: The fourth line of Zack MacEwen, Teddy Blueger and Brandon Duhaime stepped up in a big way as the Maple Leafs beat the Rangers.
items.body: TORONTO — There was a moment, five minutes into the night, when it looked like this game might turn. The Toronto Maple Leafs had struck out to an early lead against the visiting New York Rangers, off another moment of brilliance from young Easton Cowan. But the Blueshirts had started pushing back, piling up chances. A Vladislav Gavrikov point shot had glanced off Mika Zibanejad’s stick and beaten Sergei Bobrovsky, quieting the Scotiabank Arena crowd. items.body: Explanation: The play on the ice was challenged under Rule 38 – Coach’s Challenge. Rule 38.1 states, “In all Coach’s Challenge situations, the original call on the ice will be overturned if, and only if, a conclusive and irrefutable determination can be made on the basis of video evidence that the original call on the ice was clearly not correct. If a review is not conclusive and/or there is any doubt whatsoever as to whether the call on the ice was correct, the original call on the ice will be confirmed.” Video review determined that Seattle’s Chandler Stephenson preceded the puck into the offensive zone and was in an off-side position prior to the goal . According to Rule 38.9, “The standard for overturning the call in the event of a “GOAL” call on the ice is that the NHL Situation Room, after reviewing any and all available replays and consulting with the On-Ice Official(s), determines that one or more Players on the attacking team preceded the puck into the attacking zone prior to the goal being scored and that, as a result, the play should have been stopped for an “Off-Side” infraction; where this standard is met, the goal will be disallowed.” The clock is reset to show 11:21 (8:39 elapsed time), when the off-side infraction occurred.

items.body: EDMONTON — Ryan Nugent-Hopkins scored the shootout winner to give the Edmonton Oilers a 6-5 victory over the Carolina Hurricanes on Thursday night. Leon Draisaitl and Connor McDavid both shone with two goals and three assists apiece for the Oilers (8-1-1) who have won three straight and seven of their last eight. McDavid sent a shot on net that deflected off Jesperi Kotkaniemi’s skate for his eighth goal of the season. McDavid, who has points in every game this season, extended his league-leading point totals to 31 in just 10 games. items.title: ‘Easy to feel special’: Troy Stecher plays hero as Maple Leafs win thriller
items.summary: If some of his previous six NHL teams took Troy Stecher for granted, the Maple Leafs have not. The undersized waiver pick-up delivered the last-minute winner in a huge win over the Rangers on Thursday.
items.body: TORONTO — As the final minute of a tied-up barnburner sizzles away, Nick Paul gets hauled down illegally by Tye Kartye in the New York Rangers’ zone but keeps the puck alive and the penalty delayed with a second effort. Brandon Duhaime gathers Paul’s loose change and feeds it back to Morgan Rielly. Thinking pass all the way, the defenceman holds the puck on his blade, drawing in weak-side winger Will Cuylle as long as possible before zipping the thing across to partner Troy Stecher . Stecher, No. 28, cuts in, snaps his first shot of the game and bulges the back of Dylan Garand’s net with just 28 seconds to go. Then the undersized waiver gem — Brad Treliving’s parting gift to a roster his predecessor overhauled something fierce — throws a fist pump high as his shot, hugs his teammates, motions for Scotiabank Arena to raise to its feet, high-fives the line, then waves to the crowd again. This time with both arms. “Dating back to last year, I’ve really embraced being a Maple Leaf. So much passion around the city and so much love for the Leafs that, as a player, it’s really hard not to feel. Like, it’s pretty easy to feel special,” says Stecher, explaining his celebration after a 5-4 thriller on Thursday. “So, just trying to bring the arena together. You know, it’s more than just us 20 in here. It’s a big-time fan base, and I feel fortunate to be a part of it.” Thing is, Stecher has felt part of something similar, way back when he was playing 20-plus minutes a night in college and earning NHL attention the undrafted way. “A way different magnitude, but I did play at North Dakota. items.body: Defenseman who 'signed here for a reason' concerned with wins, not outside noise NEWARK, N.J. -- Dougie Hamilton doesn't view his 15th NHL season as an audition or an opportunity to answer those who wondered whether his time with the New Jersey Devils was ending. After more than 900 NHL games, a few injuries, and a season in which his name circulated in trade speculation, the 33-year-old defenseman understands some judgments are out of his control. "I don't think so," Hamilton told NHL.com when asked if he entered this season feeling he had something to prove. "There's lots of different things going on, and I think for me, it's proving to yourself and doing your best. "At the end of the day, you've got to look yourself in the mirror every day. If you're putting as much work as you can and doing your best, then that's all you can do." Those familiar with Hamilton know that's a typical response, always understated but certain. He signed with New Jersey for a reason, a seven-year, $63 million contract on July 28, 2021, carrying an average annual value of $9 million through the 2027-28 season. "I mean, this is where I am; I signed here," Hamilton said. "I like being here, and I signed here for a reason. … You want to be somewhere that you're wanted and feel valued." Hamilton's name surfaced in trade rumors last season after injuries limited him to 84 games over two seasons, including a torn pectoral muscle that required surgery in 2023-24 and another injury absence in 2024-25. This season, he's looked like the player the Devils envisioned when they made him one of the NHL's highest-paid defensemen in 2021. items.body: Michigan defenseman, projected top pick, discusses adjustment to NCAA hockey, lessons from father Landon DuPont of the University of Michigan in the Big 10 will file a draft diary for NHL.com this season leading up to the 2027 NHL Draft. The 17-year-old freshman defenseman (5-foot-11, 192 pounds), who was born Calgary, is the projected No. 1 pick in the 2027 Draft. DuPont has six assists, 11 shots on goal and a plus-6 rating in five games. He had 73 points (18 goals, 55 assists) in 63 games with Everett of the Western Hockey League in 2025-26. He led all Everett defensemen with 23 points (five goals, 18 assists) in 18 WHL playoff games to help the Silvertips win the league championship and led Team Canada to a gold medal while serving as captain at the 2026 Hlinka Gretzky Cup. DuPont was the second player and first defenseman to be granted exceptional status to compete in the WHL as a 15-year-old, following Chicago Blackhawks center Connor Bedard . During Thursday night’s game against the Carolina Hurricanes , the Edmonton Oilers ‘ captain became the fourth player in NHL history to get 30 points in his first 10 games of a season with a five-point night. McDavid joins some elite company in achieving this feat, as only Mike Bossy, Wayne Gretzky and Mario Lemieux have managed to get 30 points in the first 10 games of a season. Bossy and Gretzky have only achieved the feat once, both doing so in the 1984-85 season, while Lemieux did it three times in 1988-89, 1992-93 and 1995-96, the quickest coming in 1988-89 when he hit 30 points in only eight games. Bossy and Gretzky went on to put up a respective 117 and 208 points in 1984-85, while Lemieux had 199, 160 and 161 in his three respective seasons. San Jose Sharks goalie Yaroslav Askarov made an incredible diving glove save to stop a sure goal off a rocket from Ottawa Senators forward Drake Batherson at Canadian Tire Centre on Thursday.
The Senators had a man advantage with defenseman Jake Sanderson controlling the puck
items.body: San Jose Sharks goalie Yaroslav Askarov made an incredible diving glove save to stop a sure goal off a rocket from Ottawa Senators forward Drake Batherson at Canadian Tire Centre on Thursday. The Senators had a man advantage with defenseman Jake Sanderson controlling the puck at the point. Sanderson went cross-ice to forward Tim Stutzle at the right circle. Askarov moved to his left to play a shot from Stutzle, but he opted to go back across the ice to Batherson, who had a pretty open net. Askarov, a right-hand catcher, made a huge dive to his right and snagged Batherson's shot out of midair. Even with some traffic in front of the net, Askarov was still able to get there with the dive, looking more like a Gold Glove shortstop than a hockey goalie. Earlier in the game, Askarov made a pretty nice pad save on a Shane Pinto breakaway chance. After the diving save, he laid on the ice for a second and waited for the whistle. Take the rest, Yaroslav. You earned it.

items.body: Register Login East Notes: Chatfield, Cousins, Tkachuk By Ethan Hetu | at October 22, 2026 6:35 pm The Carolina Hurricanes did a remarkable job retaining nearly the entirety of their Stanley Cup-winning roster from last season. But with another year set to go by, it seems almost certain that the club will lose at least some players from their championship roster. One player that could depart is pending UFA defenseman Jalen Chatfield . David Pagnotta of The Fourth Period reported yesterday that the Hurricanes and Chatfield’s agent, Darren Ferris of Quartexx, attempted to negotiate an extension, but those talks did not result in pen hitting paper. Pagnotta noted that there “have been no talks since” between Ferris and the Hurricanes, and added that the “inkling right now is that [Chatfield] is headed to free agency.” Chatfield, could be set to cash in on the open market after becoming a steady contributor to the Hurricanes’ defense over the last half-decade. A fleet-footed undrafted blueliner, Chatfield was plucked from the Canucks organization as a free agent and broke into the NHL after one season spent developing with Carolina’s AHL affiliate, the Chicago Wolves. After winning a Calder Cup in Chicago, Chatfield established himself at the NHL level. He was a seamless fit for the way head coach Rod Brind’Amour wants his defensemen to play, and his ability to leverage his above-average skating to close out on pucks quickly and play aggressively has made him a valuable secondary defensive piece for the club. Now 30 years old, Chatfield’s upcoming free agency represents his best chance at earning a life-changing contract. Based on Pagnotta’s reporting, it seems Chatfield might end up receiving that contract, just maybe not from the Hurricanes.

items.title: Panthers’ Cooper Black becomes tallest goalie to play NHL game
items.body: PITTSBURGH — Florida Panthers goalie Cooper Black skated onto the PPG Paints Arena ice alone during pregame warmups on Thursday night, a time-honoured hockey tradition given to rookies everywhere. It took Black fewer strides to make the memorable lap than most. Black made NHL history in his first career start when he became the tallest goaltender to ever appear in a regular-season game. Black is listed as two inches taller than Ben Bishop, Ivan Fedotov, Mads Sogaard and Mikko Koskinen, all 6-foot-7. The 25-year-old from Alpen, Michigan, who started playing when he was 8 and had a 5-inch growth spurt between his junior and senior years in high school when he shot up from 6 feet to 6 feet 5 inches and kept right on going, was excellent in his first period. Black, called up from Florida's AHL affiliate in Charlotte recently after Jacob Markstrom went down with a shoulder injury, stopped Pittsburgh Penguins defenseman Kris Letang with his blocker pad on a wrist shot about two minutes in. He also turned aside a breakaway opportunity by Penguins forward Rickard Rakell before giving up a goal to Nick Robertson, who beat Black to the glove side. Panthers head coach Paul Maurice praised Black's development in recent years. Florida signed Black as an undrafted rookie free agent in 2024. Black blossomed last season in Charlotte, posting a 25-13-4 record with a 2.47 goals against average and a .903 save percentage. “A man that size, it takes a long time to grow into that body,” Maurice said before adding with a laugh, “I think he’s done.”

This marks the second PTO for Glendening this season, as he was previously on one with the Tampa Bay Lightning. Back in late September, however, the Bolts released him from that deal. As a reminder, players are only eligible to play pre-season games with their respective clubs under a PTO. Glendening won’t be eligible to play regular-season games with the Rangers as he must sign a standard contract. The 37-year-old is a veteran of 934 NHL games, most recently playing for the Philadelphia Flyers. Glendening split 2025-26 between the Flyers and the New Jersey Devils, scoring two goals and nine points in 70 games; an appearance threshold he has reached over the past five seasons. items.body: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-USA TODAY Sports Jayne Kamin-Oncea-USA TODAY Sports Remembering The Life And Legacy Of Rangers Star Ron Duguay Ken Campbell Partner Oct 22, 2026 8:15 PM Published Oct 22, 2026 8:15 PM Updated Oct 22, 2026 8:55 PM The 12-year NHL star has passed away after a long battle with cancer. Most hockey fans remember Ron Duguay as a the perfectly coiffed cult star of the New York Rangers . And he deserves all of the recognition he gets as one of the most popular players in franchise history. But Duguay, who died of cancer at the age of 69 on Wednesday, was even more popular and dynamic as a member of the Sudbury Wolves in the mid-1970s, when he led a team that did everything but win an Ontario League championship. That was where he first displayed his blazing speed, on-ice elegance and soft touch before being drafted by the Rangers in the first round of the 1977 draft. More Videos He was truly an iconic player, one who thrived on the scene in New York. And even though he's not in the Hockey Hall of Fame, those of us from Northern Ontario will always look fondly at his No. 10, which hangs in the rafters of the Sudbury Arena.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images Positive news for the Minnesota Wild as they continue their road trip through Western Canada. The team activated captain Jared Spurgeon from injured reserve, making him available to be in the lineup on Thursday night, when the Wild visit the Calgary Flames . It will be the veteran defenseman’s first action in four games. He was placed on IR with an upper-body injury on Sunday, retroactive to Oct. 12, when he helped the Wild pick up a win over the Vegas Golden Knights. With Spurgeon out of the lineup, the Wild held firm, but weren’t amazing. They fell to the surprising Winnipeg Jets before beating the St. Louis Blues seven days ago. Then, after beating the Columbus Blue Jackets on Sunday, Minnesota managed to rally from a 3-1 deficit to salvage a point against the Edmonton Oilers , only to lose in overtime. In Minnesota’s first six games of the 2026-27 campaign, the 36-year-old scored a goal and four assists for five points, tied for fifth on the team in helpers. Spurgeon has a plus/minus of +4, while averaging 22:21 of ice time. Staying in the lineup and out of the press box has been tough for Spurgeon throughout his NHL career. Only one of the Edmonton native’s 17 seasons saw him appear in every game, that coming during the 2018-19 campaign. He did play in 79 games last year, which came just two years after Spurgeon was limited to a mere 16 contests. In 1.018 regular-season games in the NHL, Spurgeon has posted 124 goals and 319 assists for 443 points, with another 31 points in 84 Stanley Cup Playoff contests. items.body: 19-year-old forward lost consciousness, still 'clearly shaken,' GM says CRANBERRY, Pa. -- Ben Kindel could return to practice as soon as next week after losing consciousness aboard the Pittsburgh Penguins team plane Tuesday, general manager Kyle Dubas said Thursday. The 19-year-old forward was cleared to travel to Pittsburgh on Wednesday after experiencing a vasovagal syncope, a sudden drop in heart rate and blood pressure that reduces blood flow to the brain, about 10 minutes after the plane departed Salt Lake City International Airport. Kindel received oxygen before an emergency medical landing and was transported to the University of Utah medical center. Kindel, who played 18:53 in a 5-4 loss at the Utah Mammoth on Monday, was placed on injured reserve Thursday. He will have increased testing and could begin training in the next four days if there are no complications, Dubas said. "I mean, so tough to put a timeframe on it," Dubas said. "We play tonight. We play Saturday night. ... Our hope is to get everything done, tested, back into training here in the next four days or so and see if he can return to practice on Sunday or Monday. "That's why I would put an asterisk on that by saying 'we'll see how everything goes before then.'" Kindel has four points (two goals, two assists) in nine games this season, his second since being selected by Pittsburgh in the first round (No. 11) of the 2025 NHL Draft. He had 35 points (17 goals, 18 assists) in 77 games as a rookie. "Happy everything is alright," defenseman Erik Karlsson said. "We're moving on from that. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: David Kirouac-Imagn Images Well, this isn’t the best news if you’re a Montreal Canadiens fan. On Thursday, the team announced that captain Nick Suzuki will be out 2-4 weeks with an upper-body injury. In response, the team has called up forward Owen Beck from its American Hockey League affiliate, the Laval Rocket. While the team didn’t specify what exactly is keeping Suzuki out until November, the injury can be traced back to what happened during the Canadiens’ matchup against the San Jose Sharks on Tuesday night. In the latter half of regulation, the 27-year-old blocked a shot with his left hand, leaving him shaken up. However, Suzuki would fight through the pain, playing the remainder of the contest, which saw Montreal fall 4-3 in overtime. Not lost in Suzuki’s injury is that his career-long iron man streak will come to an end. Since first stepping onto NHL ice with the Habs during the 2019-20 campaign, Suzuki has appeared in every single one of his team’s games in both the regular season and the Stanley Cup Playoffs. He has played 546 consecutive regular-season contests, with another 56 in the postseason. Yet, Montreal will have to navigate the next few weeks, including a four-game road trip, without their on-ice leader. In nine games so far, the London, Ont. native has scored five goals and seven assists for 12 points, sitting tied for the team lead in helpers and second in goals. Beck has appeared in two games with Montreal this season, but has yet to register a point. In five games with Laval, the 22-year-old has posted a goal and an assist. items.title: Penguins’ Ben Kindel back in Pittsburgh after collapsing on team plane
items.body: Penguins forward Ben Kindel is back in Pittsburgh after collapsing on the team's plane on Tuesday. General manager Kyle Dubas told reporters on Thursday that Kindel suffered a vasovagal episode — a sudden drop in heart rate and blood pressure reducing blood flow to the brain — about 10 minutes after departing from Utah and regained consciousness after receiving oxygen from the team's medical staff. The plane made an emergency landing and Kindel was transported to the University of Utah medical centre. He was cleared to fly back to Pittsburgh on Wednesday, travelling with Nick Bonino, Jason Spezza and two team doctors. The Penguins placed the 19-year-old on injured reserve as he undergoes more testing at the team facilities. Dubas said the team hopes to get Kindel back to training within the next four days and practicing next week, depending on the results of his testing. Dubas said Kindel had no prior history of collapsing. "We will obviously follow very strict guidelines to ensure a safe return to training and play for Ben," Dubas said. "That's our primary goal and paramount to his future and health." The Coquitlam, B.C., native is in his second year with the Penguins. In nine games, Kindel has two goals and two assists. He played nearly 19 minutes during a loss to Utah on Monday night.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-US PRESSWIRE One of the game’s most iconic figures has died. On Thursday, it was announced that former NHLer Ron Duguay passed away at the age of 69 following a two-year cancer battle. The news was broken by Duguay’s girlfriend, former Alaska governor and 2008 vice presidential candidate, Sarah Palin. While Duguay may not have had hall-of-fame numbers or Stanley Cup rings, his legacy will remain one of hockey’s first stars to transcend the game, diving into popular culture with the New York Rangers during the disco-crazed 1970s. items.title: Former NHL player Ron Duguay dies at 69 after a bout with cancer
items.body: NEW YORK — Ron Duguay, who played nearly 1,000 games in the NHL from the late 1970s through the ’80s, has died of cancer. He was 69. A spokesperson for the New York Rangers said Thursday that Duguay's family informed the team of his death. Duguay played his first six seasons with the New York Rangers after they selected him with the 13th pick in the draft in 1977. The Sudbury, Ontario, native was an All-Star as a point-a-game producer in 1981-82. A series of trades led him to spend time with the Detroit Red Wings, Pittsburgh Penguins and Los Angeles Kings with another Rangers stint, as well. Duguay finished his career in the league with 673 points in the regular season and playoffs, then played in Germany and the minors. Duguay was known late in life away from hockey for dating former Alaska governor and 2008 Republican U.S. vice presidential nominee Sarah Palin. His family started a GoFundMe earlier this year to offset the costs of travel and treatments. “It’s with a shattered heart but also deep peace knowing Ron is with Jesus now,” Palin posted on social media. “He fought so hard. Love never ends.”

items.body: From steady boos to array of chants, former captain at center of emotion-filled game OTTAWA -- The scenes played out on the video board, Brady Tkachuk putting on an Ottawa Senators jersey, playing with kids, visiting hospitals, hugging teammates, doing the worm. But the words that were supposed to go along with it, the narration, couldn’t be heard at Canadian Tire Centre on Wednesday. Tkachuk, meanwhile, lifted his stick to the crowd of people determined to show their dislike and disappointment, the disillusionment they had with the player who had played for their favorite team for eight years, captained it for five, until he decided that Ottawa was not a fit for him any longer. He lifted his stick past the Florida Panthers logo on his chest, and he smiled, the grin stretching across his face, as current and former players gave him the traditional stick taps. So how did he manage the emotions of the night, the feelings surrounding the return to a place he once called home, a franchise he once belonged to, a team he once led? “It’s new,” Tkachuk said. “Those were my teammates not too long ago. New experience, once in a lifetime experience in that moment. items.title: Senators fans steal the show in Brady Tkachuk’s emotionally charged return
items.summary: When Brady Tkachuk returned to Ottawa as a despised member of the Panthers, Senators fans unleashed their combative spirit, bringing a level of sustained savagery that would make even the most vindictive fanbases proud.
items.body: KANATA, Ont. — For years, Ottawa Senators fans watched Brady Tkachuk bring the fight to opponents. When he returned to Ottawa as a despised member of the Florida Panthers, they unleashed their own combative spirit, bringing a level of sustained savagery that would make even the most vindictive fanbases proud. Sens supporters were merciless on their former captain on Wednesday night, as Tkachuk — who was traded to the Florida Panthers in June after informing Ottawa he would not sign another contract with the team — returned for the first time to the city he called home for eight seasons. The Canadian Tire Centre in Kanata throbbed with an energy worthy of a Game 7, as emotions pent up for months — maybe even longer — spilled onto the ice like blood after a brawl. While the start of the game was marked by rigorous boos, the end featured what remained of an announced sellout crowd gleefully cheering as the final seconds ticked away in a thunderous 5-1 Ottawa win. A couple events — Tkachuk himself scoring on Florida’s first shot of the contest and Sens goalie Linus Ullmark being forced out of the game with a lower-body strain in the third — threatened to sap the masses of their zealous desire to deride. items.title: Senators fans throw dozens of Brady Tkachuk jerseys on ice
items.summary: Tkachuk previously stated that he would donate any sweaters tossed on the ice to the local Boys & Girls Club.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Marc DesRosiers-Imagn Fans in the nation’s capital made their voices heard and ultimately got the last laugh. During a break in the action in the third period of the highly anticipated matchup between the Florida Panthers and Ottawa Senators , Senators fans found an opportunity to dispose of some leftover Brady Tkachuk jerseys, and dozens of sweaters from the former Ottawa captain flew over the glass and onto the ice at the Canadian Tire Centre on Wednesday night. The public display of disapproval might’ve been sparked by a scuffle involving the Tkachuk brothers, as the two got into it with many of Brady’s former teammates in front of the Ottawa bench, leading to roughing minors for the infamous duo. Senators supporters throwing jerseys on the ice was somewhat expected heading into Wednesday’s contest. After morning skate, Tkachuk told reporters he would donate any jersey thrown onto the ice to the Boys & Girls Club of Ottawa, where the 27-year-old volunteered during his time with the Sens. The players wearing the current Sens logo were sure not to let the moment overcome them, as the team put forth a dominating effort. Despite Tkachuk scoring the first goal of the game, Ottawa stormed back with five unanswered goals, coming away with a 5-1 victory. Tkachuk finished the game with a -2 plus/minus and four penalty minutes. The jersey-throwing was only part of the patrons’ antics throughout the contest. Chants of “Brady sucks,” and “F— you, Brady” came down from the rafters every time Tkachuk was on the ice. It was the fans’ first time seeing their former captain play against the Sens since he requested a trade this past offseason , with Ottawa sending him to Florida for three first-round picks and a second-round pick.

items.body: BUFFALO, N.Y. — Rookie forward Cole Knuble scored twice to help the Philadelphia Flyers beat the Buffalo Sabres 3-1 on Wednesday night. Knuble, playing his second career game, scored his first two goals in front of his father, former NHL forward Mike Knuble, who played 1,068 games with five teams. Trevor Zegras also scored and Dan Vladar made 27 saves to give the Flyers their third straight win after starting 0-6-3. Jason Zucker made his season debut following sports hernia surgery and scored for Buffalo. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen stopped 23 shots for the Sabres, who are 1-1-2 in their last four games. Sabres captain Rasmus Dahlin returned to the lineup after missing four games with an upper-body injury. The Flyers grabbed a 2-0 lead late in the first period after Knuble’s first career goal at 14:49 and a power-play goal from Zegras at 19:17 when he batted a rebound of Matvei Michkov’s shot out of the air past Luukkonen. Zucker’s power-play goal at 19:25 of the second cut it to 2-1. Knuble’s second of the game 3:03 into the third made it 3-1 after he banked in the puck off Luukkonen’s skate. Flyers forward Tyson Foerster returned to the lineup after a one-game absence because of an undisclosed injury. Both teams are in action again Saturday. In the third period of a game against the Florida Panthers on Wednesday night, Ottawa Senators goaltender Linus Ullmark left the game after suffering an apparent lower-body injury. Ullmark was hurt just a few minutes into the final period of regulation. After making a save on a long-range shot, he went to go push to his left and quickly keeled over in the butterfly position. Ullmark stayed in that position for a few minutes, while some of his teammates got into a scuffle between the benches. For Ottawa fans, seeing Ullmark injured has become the norm since he was dealt to the team in 2024. While he’s played at least over half of the games in each of his first two seasons, he has been on and off the injured list, along with taking a personal leave of absence last season. He’s already missed some time this year, as an injury against the Boston Bruins earlier this month knocked him out for one game. items.title: Senators’ Linus Ullmark exits vs. Panthers with apparent injury
items.body: The Ottawa Senators once again lost their starting netminder to an apparent injury on Wednesday against the Florida Panthers. Linus Ullmark had to be helped off by a trainer and teammate Claude Giroux after staying down on the ice following a third-period save. The stop came on a shot off the rush from former Senators captain Brady Tkachuk. But as the rebound went to an Ottawa defenceman and down to the Florida end, Ullmark hunched over in pain as officials blew the play dead. As the Senators goalie was tended to in his crease, a scrum broke out in front of the Ottawa bench while the home fans continued their game-long chant of "Brady sucks" and threw Tkachuk jerseys on the ice. Ullmark had stopped 16 of the 17 shots he faced before exiting. This is the second time this month that the 33-year-old wasn't able to finish a start after leaving early against the Boston Bruins on Oct. 5. Senators head coach Travis Green said Ullmark "tweaked something a little bit" in that outing against Boston. Ullmark entered Wednesday's game with a 6-1-0 record on the season with a 1.33 goals-against average and .945 save percentage.

items.body: Register Login Latest On Quinn Hughes’ Future With Wild By Ethan Hetu | at October 21, 2026 9:00 pm The Minnesota Wild have been here before. A little over a year ago, their best player, Kirill Kaprizov , was a pending unrestricted free agent. Every conversation about the team had Kaprizov’s shadow looming over it, until he eventually signed a massive eight-year, $17MM AAV deal. Wild fans could not be blamed for feeling a sense of déjà vu right now, as star defenseman Quinn Hughes is arguably the team’s best player, and is approaching UFA status in the summer without a contract extension in place. The key difference, though, is that by this point in the year, Kaprizov had already signed his extension. Hughes has not. Entering the season, Hughes addressed his contract status with the Wild , telling the media that his extension would “be done whenever I feel like it needs to be done.” He added that he does not feel “backed up against a wall” needing to rush into signing a new contract, and that any delay is because he “want[s] to make sure I’m taking my time on everything and make sure I’m making a decision that is going to be good for everyone.” Earlier in the summer , key decision-makers in Minnesota projected public confidence that Hughes would eventually re-sign with the club. Talks were ongoing, but by August, GM Bill Guerin did publicly acknowledge that a deal may not be imminent, saying on a radio appearance that “these things take time.” It’s now nearly a month into the NHL season, and no deal has materialized. While that should most certainly not be taken as an indication that Hughes has made up his mind and will not extend with the Wild, it is still notable that he remains a pending UFA. A full contract never materialized, though, and now Brown has finally found a landing spot to begin his season. According to an official announcement , Brown has signed with HC Ajoie, who are based in Porrentruy, Switzerland and compete in Switzerland’s National League. Brown signed a contract that will last until the end of the 2026 calendar year. The deal contains an option to extend for the rest of the 2026-27 season. Brown is set to join a roster with several former NHL players, including former AHL MVP Daniel Carr and former Dallas Stars top prospect Julius Honka . Brown, 28, is set to begin his European pro career as a result of this signing. His professional career thus far has been spent entirely in the NHL and AHL. Last season, Brown played 31 games for the AHL’s Ontario Reign, scoring 16 points. The 2016 No. 11 overall pick has 99 NHL games and 26 points on his resume.

items.title: Canucks GM Ryan Johnson preaching patience as losses pile up
items.summary: With the rebuilding Canucks on an eight-game losing streak, GM Ryan Johnson isn’t panicking. “Before it gets better, it was going to get really hard, and we have to understand that.”
items.body: VANCOUVER — The evening before training camp opened, general manager Ryan Johnson gathered the Vancouver Canucks ’ staff and players for a dinner meeting at the team’s lakeside hotel in Penticton, and then spoke the truth. “The No. 1 thing I talked about is: ‘You have no idea how hard this is going to be,’” Johnson recalled Wednesday. “Like, ‘what you've signed up for here is almost impossible.’ You’d be ignorant... if you thought you were just going to walk in and things would fall into place. I said: ‘You’ve got to be ready because you're going to get punched in the face real quick.’ Here they are, bruised and spiralling through an eight-game losing streak and just 2-8-1 through the start of the rebuild’s first full season. In their last five games, Vancouver has been tied or led four times through 40 minutes and trailed (by a goal) once, then been outscored 11-0 in the third period while losing all of them. The rebuild is not the impossible part that Johnson referred to just five weeks ago, although there is overwhelming evidence around the National Hockey League — see the Detroit Red Wings, the Canucks’ opponents Thursday — that it will be difficult. The impossible part is believing the Canucks, under new management, with new coaches and new systems, many young and new players, and lofty organizational priorities regarding culture and environment, would somehow come out of the gate and be successful competitively against a murderer’s row of initial opponents. In seven of their first 11 games, the Canucks have faced a team that has either won the Stanley Cup or been to the final in the last five years. And like 7-Eleven, the Canucks’ team defence has been open at all hours, surrendering an NHL-worst 51 goals. As Johnson predicted, they have been punched in the face.

items.title: Tkachuk heavily booed by Ottawa crowd in return with Panthers
items.body: A Wednesday night game in October wouldn't normally attract much attention for the Ottawa Senators . But this one was different. Former captain Brady Tkachuk was heavily booed in his return to Ottawa as a member of the Florida Panthers , four months after requesting a trade from the only NHL team he'd ever known. Spectators also drowned out a video tribute to the former captain with profane chants. Tkachuk seemed to revel in the atmosphere. He raised his stick in acknowledgement during the tribute and waved at fans with his trademark grin. Drafted fourth overall in 2018, Tkachuk spent eight seasons with the Senators. A fan favourite for much of his tenure, he helped Ottawa return to the playoffs in 2025, ending a seven-year drought. Tkachuk opened the scoring with a power-play goal midway through the first period. His relationship with some fans grew strained last season. Tkachuk and his brother Matthew faced criticism over their "Wingmen" podcast, while Brady's decision to attend a White House celebration following the U.S. men's Olympic gold medal also drew backlash. Speculation about Tkachuk's future in Ottawa intensified late last season. At the team's season-ending press conference in April, he acknowledged the rumours had become a distraction, insisting, "I have been fully committed to this team." Less than two months later, Tkachuk was traded to the Panthers. "I've talked about it a lot that, you know, there's professional reasons, personal reasons why I wasn't going to re-sign here, and a lot of those things have remained private between (Senators GM Steve Staios) and I," Tkachuk said. items.summary: Tkachuk explained ahead of his return to Ottawa Wednesday that there were both personal and professional reasons he would not have re-signed with the Senators.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect When the NHL schedule was released over the summer, Oct. 21 stood out immediately due to the matchup in Canada’s capital between the Ottawa Senators and Florida Panthers , set to mark Brady Tkachuk’s return to Ottawa after he requested and received a trade in June. On Wednesday night, after a few months of waiting, the Ottawa faithful had their chance to let their former captain know how they felt about his decision. To the surprise of absolutely nobody, Tkachuk was showered with boos – and, of course, “Brady Sucks” chants prior to the game. Senators general manager Steve Staios revealed shortly after the trade, which took place during the 2026 NHL Draft, that Tkachuk had specifically requested to be moved elsewhere. Before the game on Wednesday, Tkachuk addressed reporters , citing both personal and professional reasons that he had no plans to re-sign with the Senators upon the conclusion of his contract. Still, Tkachuk attempted to strike a conciliatory tone with the fans who once adored him. The younger Tkachuk brother got off to a slow start with his new team before making his presence felt in historic fashion last week. items.body: Register Login Carolina Hurricanes Activate Seth Jarvis By Brennan McClain | at October 21, 2026 5:55 pm The defending Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes will return their best goal-scorer from the past two years tomorrow night. According to a team announcement , the Hurricanes activated forward Seth Jarvis from the injured reserve. Jarvis, 24, underwent shoulder surgery in late June, shortly after Carolina lifted its second Stanley Cup in franchise history. Originally, Jarvis was given a recovery timeline of four to six months. Returning tomorrow, Jarvis will have missed approximately three months and three weeks. Although he’ll need time to regain his form, Jarvis’ return is a big boost for a team dead-set on repeating as champions this season. Even without one of their top offensive talents, the Hurricanes have earned an 8-2-1 record through their first 11 contests of the 2026-27 campaign. The former 13th overall pick blossomed into the player he is today nearly four years ago. Since the beginning of the 2023-24 campaign, Jarvis has scored 97 goals and 200 points in 225 games with a +41 rating, averaging nearly 19 minutes of ice time per game. He has also regularly received votes for the Selke Trophy and is uncommonly physical for a first-line winger. In last year’s postseason, Carolina was mostly driven by their electric line of Jackson Blake , Logan Stankoven , and Taylor Hall , who scored 25 goals and 55 points in 57 games combined. However, Jarvis contributed plenty, scoring four goals and 11 points in 19 games, including the overtime-winning goal in Game 2 against the Vegas Golden Knights in the Stanley Cup Final. On Wednesday, the team announced that winger Seth Jarvis has been activated off injured reserve. In addition, Carolina has called up forward Skyler Brind’Amour from their American Hockey League (AHL) affiliate Chicago Wolves while sending down forward Bradley Nadeau. Last season, the Winnipeg native had 32 goals and 34 assists for 66 points in 71 games, and then contributed four goals and seven assists for 11 points in 19 playoff games en route to the Hurricanes winning the Stanley Cup. He also put up no goals and one assist in five games for the silver medal-winning Canadian men’s national team at the 2026 Milano Cortina Winter Olympics in February. Selected 13th overall by Carolina in the 2020 NHL Entry Draft, Jarvis immediately proved he belonged in the NHL with 40 points in his rookie season of 2021-22, finishing 13th in voting for the Calder Trophy.
